Usually, in these games, the effective force is the sum of (attack * count) for attacker, and (defense * count) for defender, with counter bonus if the most numerous type counters the defender's most numerous type.

"The winner also takes losses (attrition against the loser's effective force)."
How is attrition calculated?
Usually, the loser loses all troops, and the winner loses some troops proportional to the defender's effective force.

Let's look at the combat rules:
"When you ATTACK, your troops count their ATTACK; the DEFENDER counts the DEFENSE of theirs.
Counter triangle (a BONUS, not an automatic win): spearman counters knight; archer counters spearman; knight counters archer. Having the counter multiplies your force by 1.5.
The MOST NUMEROUS type of each army sets the counter matchup (ties in count break in the order spearman, archer, knight).
Defending is easier: defense counts x1.25 in a village and x1.5 in a castle (capital). In the open field (on a road) there is no bonus.
The side with the HIGHER effective force wins. A tie favors the DEFENDER.
The winner also takes losses (attrition against the loser's effective force)."

Can a single village send multiple armies to different destinations in the same turn?
Usually, in these games, a village can only send one army per turn, or it can send multiple if it has enough troops, but let's look at the rules carefully:
"An army STOPS at the first village on its path that is not yours and fights there, even if you ordered a more distant destination."
"Troops sent from DIFFERENT villages never add up, even when they arrive at the same target on the same turn: each send fights alone, one at a time."
This implies that troops from the SAME village to the SAME target would add up, but since they are from the same village, they are just one army.
But can we split the garrison of one village into two armies and send them to two different targets?
Let's think. In standard campaign games, you can only issue one movement order per village per turn, or you can split. But the prompt says:
"movements": [ {"fromId": <id of one of YOUR villages>, "toId": <id of ANY other village...}, ... ]
The JSON schema allows multiple movements from the same village in the list, but usually, a village has a single garrison and you decide how much to send. If you send some to A and some to B, they are split.

This means if we send 3 armies to Badajoz, they will fight the garrison one after another.
Is that good or bad?
If the first army defeats the garrison completely, the other two armies will arrive at an empty village (or rather, the conquered village) and just join it. But if the first army doesn't defeat the garrison completely, the second army will fight the remaining garrison (which might have been reinforced or not, but since it's simultaneous, the garrison doesn't get reinforcements during the turn, but the first army's losses will be applied, and the second army will fight the survivors).
Actually, sending multiple armies to the same target on the same turn is extremely powerful because they fight sequentially, effectively doubling or tripling our total attacking force while the defender has to fight them one by one!
